actinolite.name: Actinolite
actinolite.color: Dark Green / Emerald to Blackish Green
actinolite.economic_value: Industrial Asbestos / Gem Nephrite Jade Component
actinolite.description: Elongated prismatic to fibrous green amphibole mineral found in greenschist facies metamorphic rocks.
actinolite.identification_tips: Distinct bladed green crystals forming radiating sheaves; vitreous luster.

aegirine.name: Aegirine
aegirine.color: Dark Green / Brownish Black / Jet Black
aegirine.economic_value: Collector Gem Specimen & Alkaline Rock Indicator
aegirine.description: Sodium iron clinopyroxene occurring in alkali-rich igneous rocks and nepheline syenite pegmatites.
aegirine.identification_tips: Slender, sharply terminated prismatic black-green needles with steep terminations.

agate.name: Agate
agate.color: Multicolor Banded (White, Red, Brown, Blue, Gray)
agate.description: Microcrystalline variety of silica characterized by fineness of grain and brightness of color bands.
agate.identification_tips: Concentric multi-colored banding and waxy translucent luster with conchoidal fracture.

albite.name: Albite (Sodium Feldspar)
albite.economic_value: Ceramic Glazes, Glassmaking & Pegmatite Host Indicator
albite.description: Sodium endmember of plagioclase feldspar group forming bladed crystals known as cleavelandite in pegmatites.
albite.identification_tips: Triclinic cleavage striations on {001} cleavage faces; pearly luster on cleavage planes.

almandine.name: Almandine Garnet
almandine.color: Deep Red / Brownish Red / Purplish Black
almandine.description: Iron aluminum garnet, the most common species of garnet, forming dodecahedral crystals in mica schists.
almandine.identification_tips: Rhombic dodecahedral crystal habit, extreme hardness (scratches glass readily), high density.

amazonite.name: Amazonite
amazonite.description: Vibrant green-blue variety of potassium feldspar (microcline) colored by trace lead and water impurities.
amazonite.identification_tips: Characteristic grid-like perthitic white striations running through turquoise-green matrix.

amber.name: Amber
amber.description: Fossilized tree resin valued since antiquity for its warm color, lightweight feel, and bio-inclusions.
amber.identification_tips: Extremely light (floats in concentrated saltwater), develops negative static electricity when rubbed.

amethyst.name: Amethyst
amethyst.description: Purple quartz colored by natural gamma irradiation of trivalent iron impurities in the crystal lattice.
amethyst.identification_tips: Hexagonal prisms with pyramid terminations; rich purple zoning; scratches feldspar easily.

andalusite.name: Andalusite (Chiastolite)
andalusite.description: Aluminium nesosilicate polymorph found in regional and thermal metamorphic pelitic rocks.
andalusite.identification_tips: Strong green-to-red pleochroism under rotating light; square prismatic cross-sections with cross inclusions.

andradite.name: Andradite (Demantoid Garnet)
andradite.economic_value: Extreme Value Gemstone (Dispersion higher than Diamond)
andradite.description: Calcium-iron garnet group mineral famous for its demantoid variety exhibiting horsetail inclusions and fiery dispersion.
andradite.identification_tips: Adamantine brilliance, higher dispersion fire than diamond, isometric dodecahedral crystals.

anorthite.name: Anorthite (Calcium Feldspar)
anorthite.economic_value: Industrial Ceramic Refractory & Igneous Layering Indicator
anorthite.description: Calcium endmember of plagioclase feldspar series dominant in basic igneous rocks and lunar highland crust.
anorthite.identification_tips: Dense white cleavage blocks; readily attacked by hydrochloric acid leaving silica gel residue.

apatite.name: Apatite (Phosphate)
apatite.color: Sea Green / Neon Blue / Yellow / Violet
apatite.economic_value: Agricultural Phosphorus Fertilizer & Neon Gem Specimen
apatite.description: Principal source of phosphorus worldwide, forming stunning hexagonal prisms in carbonatites and pegmatites.
apatite.identification_tips: Standard 5 on Mohs scale (can be scratched with a knife blade); hexagonal prism terminations.

arfvedsonite.name: Arfvedsonite
arfvedsonite.economic_value: Collector Gem Material & Rare Earth Host Petrological Marker
arfvedsonite.description: Sodium amphibole mineral occurring in peralkaline igneous syenites, showing striking blue-bronze chatoyancy.
arfvedsonite.identification_tips: Prismatic black blades exhibiting distinct peacock-blue to bronze flashes when tilted in light.

arsenopyrite.name: Arsenopyrite (Mispickel)
arsenopyrite.economic_value: Primary Ore of Arsenic & Major Refractory Gold Host
arsenopyrite.toxicity: Highly Toxic (Arsenic content; wash hands after handling)
arsenopyrite.description: Iron arsenic sulfide mineral and the most widespread arsenic mineral, intimately associated with hydrothermal gold deposits.
arsenopyrite.identification_tips: Emits strong garlic (arsenic) odor when struck with hammer; silvery metallic luster with high density.

azurite.name: Azurite (Chessylite)
azurite.color: Deep Azure Blue / Royal Navy Blue
azurite.economic_value: Copper Ore Indicator & Elite Mineral Specimen
azurite.toxicity: Toxic if inhaled as cutting dust (Copper)
azurite.description: Vibrant blue basic copper carbonate mineral formed by weathering and oxidation of copper sulfide ore bodies.
azurite.identification_tips: Intense deep azure blue color; effervesces vigorously in dilute hydrochloric acid with blue streak.

barite.name: Barite (Baryte)
barite.color: Colorless / White / Golden Yellow / Sky Blue
barite.economic_value: Oil & Gas Drilling Mud Weighting Agent
barite.description: Barium sulfate mineral renowned for its exceptionally high specific gravity despite its non-metallic glassy appearance.
barite.identification_tips: Remarkably heavy feel in hand (heavy spar); perfect tabular crystals with pearly cleavage planes.

bastnasite.name: Bastnäsite (Rare Earth Ore)
bastnasite.color: Honey Yellow / Reddish Brown / Wax Yellow
bastnasite.economic_value: Critical Strategic Ore for Neodymium, Cerium & Lanthanum
bastnasite.toxicity: Weakly radioactive due to trace Thorium
bastnasite.description: Fluorocarbonate mineral that constitutes the world's primary commercial source of light rare earth elements (LREEs).
bastnasite.identification_tips: High specific gravity, greasy-to-adamantine luster, dissolves slowly in warm acid with effervescence.

beryl.name: Beryl (Emerald / Aquamarine)
beryl.economic_value: World Class Precious Gemstone & Source of Strategic Beryllium Metal
beryl.toxicity: Non-toxic in solid state (Beryllium dust toxic if cut without water)
beryl.description: Beryllium aluminium cyclosilicate occurring in granite pegmatites and mica schists, yielding world-famous gemstones.
beryl.identification_tips: Classic 6-sided hexagonal prism with flat pinacoid basal terminations; hard enough to scratch quartz.

biotite.name: Biotite (Black Mica)
biotite.economic_value: Industrial Electrical Insulation & Geochronological Age Dating
biotite.description: Common dark phyllosilicate mica mineral found in granites, gneisses, and schists, cleaving into elastic sheets.
biotite.identification_tips: Splits effortlessly with a fingernail into thin, dark, flexible, and elastic transparent sheets.

bornite.name: Bornite (Peacock Ore)
bornite.color: Copper-Red to Bronze (Tarnishes to Iridescent Purple/Blue)
bornite.economic_value: Major Copper Ore (contains 63.3% Copper by weight)
bornite.description: Crucial copper iron sulfide mineral known as peacock ore due to its spectacular iridescent purple-blue surface tarnish.
bornite.identification_tips: Bronze-brown fresh fracture that rapidly tarnishes into vibrant rainbow purple-blue sheen; metallic.

calcite.name: Calcite (Iceland Spar)
calcite.economic_value: Cement, Lime, Agricultural Fertilizer & Optical Polarization
calcite.description: Calcium carbonate mineral forming limestone, marble, and cave stalactites, showing spectacular double refraction.
calcite.identification_tips: Fizzes instantly and vigorously in cold dilute hydrochloric acid; breaks into perfect rhombohedrons.

carnelian.name: Carnelian
carnelian.description: Semi-precious reddish-orange variety of microcrystalline chalcedony colored by iron oxide (hematite) nanoinclusions.
carnelian.identification_tips: Warm translucent reddish-orange glow with waxy luster; harder than steel knife blade.

carrollite.name: Carrollite (Cobalt-Copper Sulfide)
carrollite.color: Light Steel-Gray to Silver with Reddish Tarnish
carrollite.economic_value: Premier Strategic Cobalt Ore for EV Lithium Batteries & High-Value Specimens
carrollite.toxicity: Contains Cobalt and Nickel; handle with care
carrollite.description: Sulfide of copper and cobalt, forming world-renowned mirror-metallic octahedrons in the Central African Copperbelt.
carrollite.identification_tips: Flawless mirror-like octahedral metallic crystals; steel-gray with brilliant metallic luster.

cassiterite.name: Cassiterite (Tin Stone)
cassiterite.economic_value: Chief Ore of Tin Metal used in Electronics Soldering and Tinplating
cassiterite.description: Heavy, metallic to adamantine tin dioxide mineral, famous for elbow knee-twin crystals in hydrothermal veins and placer gravels.
cassiterite.identification_tips: Remarkably high density (heavy tin stone); elbow-twinned crystals; adamantine luster; zinc test turns gray coating.

celestine.name: Celestine (Celestite)
celestine.color: Sky Blue / Pale Blue / Colorless / White
celestine.economic_value: Primary Source of Strontium for Fireworks & Pyrotechnics
celestine.description: Strontium sulfate mineral named for its delicate heavenly sky-blue crystal geodes found abundantly in Madagascar.
celestine.identification_tips: Delicate sky-blue color, heavy feel for a light mineral, perfect orthorhombic prismatic crystals.

cerussite.name: Cerussite (White Lead Ore)
cerussite.economic_value: Important Lead Ore & Elite Reticulated Gem Specimen
cerussite.toxicity: Toxic if ingested or inhaled (Lead content)
cerussite.description: Secondary lead carbonate mineral famous for its brilliant diamond-like luster and snowflake reticulated twinning.
cerussite.identification_tips: Extremely heavy; brilliant adamantine luster; fizzes with effervescence in warm dilute nitric acid.

chalcedony.name: Chalcedony
chalcedony.description: Cryptocrystalline form of silica composed of microscopic intergrowths of quartz and moganite.
chalcedony.identification_tips: Botryoidal (grape-like) rounded crusts; translucent waxy luster; conchoidal sharp fracture.

chalcocite.name: Chalcocite (Copper Glance)
chalcocite.description: Important supergene copper sulfide mineral formed in the enrichment zones of copper deposits.
chalcocite.identification_tips: Sectile (can be cut with a pocket knife leaving shiny metallic surface); dark lead-gray metallic color.

chalcopyrite.name: Chalcopyrite (Copper Pyrite)
chalcopyrite.economic_value: World's Primary Source of Copper Metal (34.5% Cu)
chalcopyrite.description: The most widely distributed copper mineral, forming golden brassy sphenoidal crystals in hydrothermal veins.
chalcopyrite.identification_tips: Easily scratched by a knife (unlike pyrite which is harder than 6); distinct greenish-black streak.

chromite.name: Chromite
african_regions: Bushveld Igneous Complex (South Africa - 70% of World Reserves)
chromite.economic_value: Exclusive Commercial Source of Chromium for Stainless Steel & Superalloys
chromite.description: Iron chromium oxide mineral belonging to the spinel group, occurring in stratiform layered ultramafic intrusions.
chromite.identification_tips: Heavy black granular masses; dark brown streak; weakly magnetic or non-magnetic.

chrysoberyl.name: Chrysoberyl (Alexandrite / Cat's Eye)
chrysoberyl.economic_value: Elite Precious Gemstone (Alexandrite: Green in daylight, red in incandescent)
chrysoberyl.description: Extremely hard beryllium aluminate mineral prized for its trilling cyclic twins, cymophane chatoyancy, and color-change alexandrite.
chrysoberyl.identification_tips: Scratches topaz (hardness 8.5); cyclic six-ling pseudo-hexagonal twinned crystals; high adamantine brilliance.

chrysoprase.name: Chrysoprase
chrysoprase.color: Apple Green / Vibrant Emerald Lime Green
chrysoprase.economic_value: Highest Value Variety of Chalcedony for Fine Jewelry
chrysoprase.description: Precious variety of chalcedony silica colored by trace quantities of hydrated nickel silicate (willemseite/garnierite).
chrysoprase.identification_tips: Distinct uniform apple-green color; smooth waxy translucent surface with conchoidal fracture.

cobaltite.name: Cobaltite
cobaltite.economic_value: Crucial Source of Strategic Cobalt Metal for Aerospace & Batteries
cobaltite.description: Cobalt arsenic sulfide mineral found in high-temperature hydrothermal deposits, forming striate pyritohedral cubes.
cobaltite.identification_tips: Silver-white metallic cubes and pyritohedrons with faint pink/violet iridescent tarnish.

columbite.name: Columbite (Coltan / Niobite)
african_regions: Kivu Region (DR Congo - Major Global Supplier)
columbite.economic_value: Essential Strategic Metal (Niobium) for Superconductors, Capacitors & Smart Devices
columbite.toxicity: Weakly radioactive due to trace Thorium/Uranium
columbite.description: Black oxide mineral series of niobium and tantalum, crucial to modern electronics and smartphone micro-capacitors.
columbite.identification_tips: High density, sub-metallic black tabular crystals; reddish-black streak; resistant to acid attack.

copper.name: Native Copper
copper.color: Copper-Red / Rose Red (Tarnishes to Brown / Green Malachite)
copper.economic_value: Premier Electrical Conductor Metal & Prized Mineral Specimen
copper.description: Naturally occurring uncombined metallic copper forming dendritic branch-like and arborescent skeletal crystal aggregates.
copper.identification_tips: Extremely malleable (bends without breaking); heavy copper-red metallic luster; leaves shiny metallic mark.

corundum.name: Corundum (Sapphire / Ruby)
corundum.color: Pigeon Blood Red (Ruby) / Royal Blue (Sapphire) / Yellow / Pink
corundum.economic_value: World Leading Precious Gemstone (Ruby & Sapphire) & Industrial Abrasive
corundum.description: Crystalline form of aluminum oxide, second only to diamond in hardness, yielding the cardinal gemstones Ruby and Sapphire.
corundum.identification_tips: Scratches all minerals except diamond (Hardness 9); barrel-shaped hexagonal hexagonal prisms; dense.

cuprite.name: Cuprite (Ruby Copper)
cuprite.color: Cochnieal Red / Crimson / Adamantine Ruby Red
cuprite.economic_value: High Copper Content Ore (88.8% Cu) & Prized Gem Specimen
cuprite.description: Secondary copper oxide mineral formed in oxidized copper deposits, famous for giant gemmy octahedral crystals from Namibia.
cuprite.identification_tips: Brilliant adamantine red internal reflections; brownish-red streak; heavy octahedral crystals.

diamond.name: Diamond
diamond.color: Colorless / Fancy Yellow / Pink / Blue / Green
diamond.economic_value: Supreme Luxury Gemstone & Industrial Ultra-Precision Cutting Material
diamond.description: Pure carbon crystallized in the isometric system under extreme mantle pressures, famous for unmatched hardness and fire.
diamond.identification_tips: Hardness 10 (scratches all known substances); supreme adamantine luster; perfect octahedral cleavage.

diopside.name: Diopside (Chrome Diopside)
diopside.economic_value: Vibrant Green Gemstone & Diamond Exploration Pathfinder Mineral
diopside.description: Monoclinic pyroxene mineral forming intense emerald-green gem crystals when rich in chromium, found in kimberlites.
diopside.identification_tips: Intense rich chrome-green color; prismatic 4-sided cross sections with right-angle pyroxene cleavage.

dolomite.name: Dolomite
dolomite.economic_value: Refractory Magnesium Source, Building Stone & Ore Host Rock
dolomite.description: Anhydrous carbonate mineral composed of calcium magnesium carbonate, forming curved saddle-shaped crystals.
dolomite.identification_tips: Does NOT fizz in cold acid (unlike calcite), but fizzes vigorously in warm acid or when powdered.

epidote.name: Epidote (Pistacite)
epidote.economic_value: Collector Gem Specimen & Hydrothermal Alteration Marker
epidote.description: Silicate mineral characterized by its distinctive pistachio-green color, abundant in contact metamorphic skarns.
epidote.identification_tips: Unique pistachio-green yellowish color; elongated prismatic crystals with striations.

eudialyte.name: Eudialyte
eudialyte.economic_value: Strategic Zirconium, Hafnium & Heavy Rare Earth Ore (HREE)
eudialyte.toxicity: Weakly radioactive due to trace Rare Earths
eudialyte.description: Complex sodium calcium zirconium silicate found in agpaitic nepheline syenites, prized for its vivid raspberry-magenta hue.
eudialyte.identification_tips: Vibrant magenta-pink patches in white/black nepheline syenite matrix; dissolves easily in acid forming silica gel.

fluorapatite.name: Fluorapatite
fluorapatite.color: Teal Blue / Neon Green / Purple / Yellow
fluorapatite.economic_value: High Grade Fertilizer Feedstock & Gem Specimens
fluorapatite.description: The most common phosphate mineral, forming flawless hexagonal tabular and prismatic gem crystals in carbonatites.
fluorapatite.identification_tips: Hexagonal prism with basal pinacoid; hardness exactly 5 (scratched by pocket knife).

fluorite.name: Fluorite (Fluorspar)
fluorite.color: Emerald Green / Royal Purple / Golden Yellow / Blue
fluorite.economic_value: Essential Metallurgical Flux & Chemical Hydrofluoric Acid Source
fluorite.description: Halide mineral composed of calcium fluoride, famous for perfect cubic crystals and strong fluorescence under UV light.
fluorite.identification_tips: Perfect 4-directional octahedral cleavage (breaks into octahedrons); cubic crystal habit; fluoresces under UV.

galena.name: Galena
galena.economic_value: World's Most Important Ore of Lead (86.6% Pb) and Major Silver Source
galena.toxicity: Toxic (Lead content; wash hands after handling)
galena.description: The primary ore mineral of lead, crystallizing in heavy, metallic, perfect cubic and octahedral forms.
galena.identification_tips: Heavy as lead; breaks into perfect smaller cubes upon impact; brilliant metallic luster and dark gray streak.

garnet.name: Garnet (General Group)
garnet.color: Deep Red / Tsavorite Green / Orange Spessartine
garnet.economic_value: Fine Jewelry Gemstones & High-Grade Industrial Waterjet Abrasives
garnet.description: Group of silicate minerals crystallized in 12-sided dodecahedral and 24-sided trapezohedral habits.
garnet.identification_tips: Distinct rhombic dodecahedron crystal habit, glass-scratching hardness, absence of cleavage.

goethite.name: Goethite (Brown Iron Ore)
goethite.economic_value: Important Iron Ore Component & Natural Ochre Pigment
goethite.description: Iron oxyhydroxide mineral formed by weathering of iron-bearing minerals, often exhibiting botryoidal velvet crusts.
goethite.identification_tips: Diagnostic mustard/yellowish-brown streak on unglazed porcelain; radial fibrous needle structure.

gold.name: Native Gold
african_regions: Witwatersrand Basin (South Africa - Largest Gold Field)
gold.economic_value: Global Monetary Standard, Fine Jewelry, Aerospace & Microelectronics
gold.description: Native precious metal celebrated across human history for its dense weight, resistance to corrosion, and supreme malleability.
gold.identification_tips: Extremely heavy; sectile and malleable (flattens under needle pressure without shattering, unlike pyrite); rich golden streak.

graphite.name: Graphite (Plumbago)
graphite.economic_value: Critical Anode Material for EV Lithium-Ion Batteries, Lubricants & Refractories
graphite.description: Naturally occurring crystalline carbon arranged in hexagonal planar sheets, famous for its extreme softness and electrical conductivity.
graphite.identification_tips: Greasy, slippery feel to the touch; marks paper and skin effortlessly with dark gray metallic streak.

grossular.name: Grossular Garnet (Tsavorite / Hessonite)
grossular.economic_value: Tsavorite is among the Most Valuable and Coveted Green Gemstones in the World
grossular.description: Calcium-aluminium garnet, famous for its vanadium-colored emerald-green tsavorite variety discovered along the Kenya-Tanzania border.
grossular.identification_tips: Intense pure vivid green fire, isometric dodecahedral crystals, absence of cleavage.

gypsum.name: Gypsum (Selenite / Desert Rose)
gypsum.economic_value: Plaster of Paris, Drywall / Sheetrock, Cement Retarder
gypsum.description: Hydrated calcium sulfate mineral, famous for clear selenite blades, satin spar fibrous masses, and desert rose rosettes.
gypsum.identification_tips: Easily scratched with a fingernail (Hardness 2); pearly cleavage surfaces; desert rose rosette habit.

halite.name: Halite (Rock Salt)
halite.economic_value: Human Nutrition, Chemical Chlorine / Soda Ash Production
halite.description: Common sodium chloride mineral, crystallizing into perfect transparent cubes in arid salt pans and playas.
halite.identification_tips: Characteristic salty taste; perfect 90° cubic cleavage; dissolves readily in water.

hematite.name: Hematite (Kidney Ore)
hematite.color: Metallic Steel-Gray / Rust Red / Mirror Black (Specular)
african_regions: Simandou Iron Ore Range (Guinea - World's Largest Undeveloped Deposit)
hematite.economic_value: Primary Source of Iron Metal for Global Steel Industry (70% Fe)
hematite.description: The chief iron ore mineral, occurring as metallic specular plates, botryoidal kidney ore, or red earthy masses.
hematite.identification_tips: Diagnostic cherry-red to blood-red streak on porcelain plate regardless of metallic black surface color.

kaolinite.name: Kaolinite (China Clay)
kaolinite.economic_value: Paper Coating, Fine Porcelain Ceramics & Cosmetics
kaolinite.description: Layered silicate clay mineral produced by the hydrothermal alteration or chemical weathering of aluminum silicate minerals like feldspar.
kaolinite.identification_tips: Earthy chalky smell when breathed upon; sticks slightly to tongue; soft white powdery clay mass.

kyanite.name: Kyanite (Disthene)
kyanite.color: Bladed Sapphire Blue / Cyan / White / Green
kyanite.economic_value: Industrial High-Refractory Spark Plugs & Striking Blue Gemstones
kyanite.description: Blue bladed aluminosilicate mineral famous for its variable directional hardness (anisotropic hardness).
kyanite.identification_tips: Elongated sapphire-blue blades; can be scratched with knife parallel to length, but scratches knife across width.

labradorite.name: Labradorite (Spectrolite)
labradorite.color: Dark Gray with Iridescent Blue/Gold/Green Labradorescence
african_regions: Tuléar & Fort Dauphin (Madagascar - World Premier Source)
labradorite.economic_value: High Value Ornamental Stone, Countertops & Fine Jewelry
labradorite.description: Intermediate plagioclase feldspar displaying spectacular optical play of color known as labradorescence.
labradorite.identification_tips: Brilliant peacock-blue and golden-orange spectral flashes (labradorescence) appearing when rotated in light.

lapis_lazuli.name: Lapis Lazuli
lapis_lazuli.color: Deep Ultramarine Blue with Golden Pyrite Flecks
lapis_lazuli.economic_value: Historic Ultramarine Pigment, Royal Ornaments & Fine Jewelry
lapis_lazuli.description: Deep blue metamorphic rock prized since Egyptian antiquity, composed primarily of lazurite with sparkling pyrite stars.
lapis_lazuli.identification_tips: Rich celestial ultramarine blue color speckled with golden metallic pyrite grains and white calcite veins.

magnetite.name: Magnetite (Lodestone)
magnetite.economic_value: Key Iron Ore (72.4% Fe) & Natural Ferromagnetic Material
magnetite.description: Ferrimagnetic iron oxide mineral and the most magnetic of all naturally occurring minerals on Earth.
magnetite.identification_tips: Strongly attracted to a magnet (or acts as a permanent magnet / lodestone); black streak; octahedral crystals.

malachite.name: Malachite
malachite.toxicity: Toxic if inhaled as dust (Copper content)
malachite.description: Secondary copper mineral famous for its vibrant green color and banded circular concentric patterns.
malachite.identification_tips: Effervesces vigorously with cold dilute hydrochloric acid. Green streak on porcelain plate.

opal.name: Opal (Welo Fire Opal)
opal.color: Play-of-Color (Rainbow Spectral Flashes on White/Amber Body)
african_regions: Welo / Wollo Province (Ethiopia - World Leader in Hydrophane Opal)
opal.economic_value: High-Value Fine Jewelry Gemstone displaying optical diffraction play-of-color
opal.description: Hydrated amorphous form of silica exhibiting vivid three-dimensional rainbow play-of-color due to diffraction grating spheres.
opal.identification_tips: Spectacular rainbow flashes moving across body; lightweight; hydrophane property (absorbs water).

pyrite.name: Pyrite (Fool's Gold)
pyrite.economic_value: Sulfuric Acid Manufacturing, Semiconductor Research & Gold Host
pyrite.toxicity: Non-toxic (Can generate acid mine drainage if exposed to water/air)
pyrite.description: Iron sulfide mineral nicknamed Fool's Gold due to its brassy color and bright metallic luster, forming perfect cubes and pyritohedrons.
pyrite.identification_tips: Hard enough to strike sparks against steel (Hardness > 6); brittle (shatters into black powder, unlike malleable gold).

quartz.name: Quartz (Rock Crystal)
quartz.rarity_tier: Second Most Abundant Mineral in Earth's Continental Crust
quartz.economic_value: Semiconductor Silicon Wafers, Electronics Piezoelectric Oscillators, Solar Panels
quartz.toxicity: Non-toxic (Respirable silica dust hazard if cut dry)
quartz.description: Hard crystalline mineral composed of silicon and oxygen atoms linked in a continuous framework of SiO₄ tetrahedra.
quartz.identification_tips: Hardness exactly 7 (scratches glass and steel knife); hexagonal prisms with 6-sided pyramid terminations; conchoidal fracture.

rhodochrosite.name: Rhodochrosite (Inca Rose)
rhodochrosite.color: Vibrant Raspberry Rose / Crimson Red / Banded Pink
african_regions: N'Chwaning Mines I, II & Wessels Mine, Kalahari (South Africa - World's Finest Red Scalenohedrons)
rhodochrosite.economic_value: Minor Manganese Ore & World-Class Collector Crystal Mineral
rhodochrosite.description: Manganese carbonate mineral famous for deep cherry-red scalenohedral crystals produced in the Kalahari Manganese Field.
rhodochrosite.identification_tips: Stunning intense raspberry/rose-red color; rhombohedral cleavage; effervesces in warm dilute hydrochloric acid.

tanzanite.name: Tanzanite (Blue Zoisite)
tanzanite.color: Vibrant Sapphire Blue / Deep Royal Violet-Purple
african_regions: Merelani Hills, Manyara Region (Tanzania - Exclusive Single Global Locality)
tanzanite.economic_value: One of the Rarest and Most Valuable Gemstones on Earth (1000x rarer than Diamond)
tanzanite.description: Blue-purple variety of zoisite colored by vanadium, found in only one small 4-kilometer strip of land in Merelani, Tanzania.
tanzanite.identification_tips: Strong trichroism (displays blue, purple, and burgundy depending on viewing angle); orthorhombic prismatic crystals.

topaz.name: Topaz (Imperial Topaz)
topaz.color: Golden Sherry / Imperial Orange / Sky Blue / Colorless
topaz.economic_value: High Value Jewelry Gemstone & Pegmatite Collector Specimen
topaz.description: Silicate mineral of aluminium and fluorine, renowned for its crystal clarity, high density, and diamond-scratching hardness.
topaz.identification_tips: Hardness 8 (cannot be scratched by quartz); perfect flat basal cleavage; diamond-like brilliance.

tourmaline.name: Tourmaline (Elbaite / Paraiba / Schorl)
tourmaline.economic_value: Paraiba Tourmaline is among the Most Valuable Gemstones in Existence; Pyroelectric Sensors
tourmaline.description: Complex boron silicate mineral famous for rounded triangular 3-sided prism cross-sections and stunning neon color zoning.
tourmaline.identification_tips: Rounded triangular cross-section (Reuleaux triangle shape); strong pleochroism; pyroelectric properties.

zircon.name: Zircon
zircon.color: Hyacinth Red / Golden Yellow / Blue / Colorless
african_regions: Richard's Bay Heavy Mineral Sands (South Africa)
zircon.economic_value: Primary Source of Zirconium & Hafnium for Nuclear Reactors & High-Fire Gemstones
zircon.toxicity: Weakly radioactive due to trace Uranium/Thorium inside lattice
zircon.description: Zirconium silicate mineral capable of surviving billions of years in Earth's crust, showing brilliance and fire close to diamond.
zircon.identification_tips: Diamond-like adamantine luster, high density, tetragonal square prism with pyramidal terminations.
